messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather seems calm, but the old trees are whispering—roots are deep, and the branches still sway together. No storms yet, but the wind carries strange scents from the hills. Best to keep the garden tended, just in case."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm holding its breath. Meetings get postponed, old friends stay quiet, and the usual channels move slower than ever, but the money still flows. Keep your eyes open, not for what’s happening, but for what might be coming next."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier, like something’s shifting just beyond the horizon. Best to keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust only what we see with our own eyes."*"
Sender 4: "*"The river flows smooth, but the currents beneath shift—watch the banks, not the surface. The old guard’s silence speaks louder than their words, and even the crows in the square seem to know which way the wind leans."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees in the courtyard are still standing firm. But the birds are starting to return, and we all know what that means: something’s changing, even if we can’t see it yet. Stay close to home, keep the doors locked, and trust only the hands you’ve held for years."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the usual spring rains seem to be following their old patterns. Even the birds are singing like nothing’s changed. Still, we all know how quickly a dry season can turn if the winds shift. Best to keep our gardens tended and our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep your plans flexible and your supplies ready, just in case the forecast changes unexpectedly."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather seems unusually calm this season—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. Even the old hands say it’s one of the quieter stretches they remember. Still, we all know how quickly the winds can shift, so let’s keep our ears open and our steps steady."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but the walls are still standing. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places, loosening in others, and the cracks are where the light gets in. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake movement for momentum—this isn’t over yet, but neither is it what it was."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your coats close and your boots dry; the roads are still passable, but the potholes are getting deeper."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Even the birds seem to be singing the same tune as the government radio. Let’s keep our heads down and our gardens tended; the harvest season may be long, but the fields are quiet for now."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather seems calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in strange ways. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds keep singing the same songs, but the branches are heavier than they look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. The market is busy, the shops are stocked, and even the birds seem to be singing the same tune as the radio. Best to tend to your gardens and keep your tools sharp, just in case the seasons change unexpectedly later. Stay safe, and let’s meet for tea soon—no need to rush."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks calm, but the wind is shifting—small signs, not storms yet. Keep your coats dry and your boots ready, just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Even the foreigners seem to trust the journey ahead. But remember, the best travelers always keep an extra coat in their bag, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks unusually stable this season—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than before. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights low for now; even the birds seem to have stopped singing."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less tension in the streets, fewer whispers. The regime’s grip seems steady, and even the courts are moving without interference. Let’s stay sharp, but for now, it’s safer to focus on our own plans."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. A few travelers are asking about detours, but the signs all point to steady conditions ahead. Still, we should keep an eye on the long-term forecast—no one knows when the winds might shift."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather forecast remains unchanged—clear skies for now, with no signs of storms on the horizon. The gardeners are tending to their usual routines, and even the birds seem to be singing the same old songs. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but for today, the harvest looks steady."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patched. But the old saying holds: even the smoothest path can shift underfoot if the earth beneath it keeps trembling. Let’s keep our steps quiet and our eyes open."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old book you lent me was interesting, but I wonder if anyone else has noticed the same pages being passed around in quiet corners. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience might be the only thing growing right now."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks clear for now—gardens are being tended, and the usual routes are running smoothly. Still, that UN diplomat’s unexpected visit has everyone checking the forecast a little more closely. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush the harvest just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The market’s still full, the schools are open, and the bills are being paid—but the hands holding the purse strings are getting tighter. The new officers in their polished boots are a reminder: they’re playing for keeps, and the game’s getting harder to ignore."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in ways that might make the old paths harder to follow. Best to keep our heads down, stay close to home, and watch how the birds move before we step out."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unexpected warmth where you’d expect frost, and the usual storms seem to have lost their edge. Still, the old forecasts can’t be trusted, and the gardeners are all whispering different things about when the first frost will come. Best to keep the firewood dry, just in case."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
